display.purpose: The stat hero on the Stats page. At most one per screen.

label.purpose: Tracked uppercase kicker above a page title. The 0.32em tracking is a signature.

wordmark.purpose: The HearthShelf lockup only: 'Hearth' in gold at 400, 'Shelf' in cream at 700.

quote.purpose: Pull-quotes and book copy. The only other place the serif appears.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Dark-theme card edge. A top highlight standing in for a lifted edge; light theme uses 0 2px 8px rgba(60,50,40,0.08).

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Popovers, menus, sheets and tooltips. Light theme uses 0 18px 48px rgba(60,50,40,0.18).

shadows.name: cover
shadows.purpose: Tile artwork. Covers are physical objects on a shelf and cast accordingly.

shadows.name: ember-throw
shadows.purpose: The primary button only. A coloured glow rather than a grey shadow, so the button reads as lit by the same fire as the room.

shadows.name: app-glow
shadows.value: radial-gradient(120% 80% at 50% -18%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--glow-accent) calc(var(--glow-strength) * 1%), transparent) 0%, transparent 62%)
shadows.purpose: The signature atmospheric bloom behind the content column, tinted live by cover art. Strength is themed: 60 dark, 14 light, 0 flat/OLED.

shadows.name: glass
shadows.purpose: The playbar and cover badges. The only blur in the system.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: The system's single easing curve. Playbar reveal/hide, sheets, and every transform-based transition.

motion.name: duration-press

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Background, colour and border transitions on hover and focus.

motion.name: duration-panel

motion.name: duration-atmosphere

motion.name: duration-car-fade
motion.purpose: Car-shell chrome fading out and waking back in.

narrative.overview:
A warm room at night with one fire in it, furnished for listening. Everything in this system follows from that single image. The fire is literal: a radial-gradient bloom (.app-glow) sits fixed behind the content column, tinted live by the current cover art, and it is the only real light source in the interface. Surfaces are warm near-neutrals stepped up from an ink base (#1b1a18) - R >= G >= B by a hair, never navy, never muddy brown - so the room reads as firelight on plaster rather than as a dark-mode inversion of a white app. Dark is home; light is a daytime option, not the default.

The room is furnished for one activity. Cover art is the only saturated colour most screens contain, and the chrome around it is deliberately quiet: fills at 6% white, hairlines at 8%, muted warm-grey type. Controls are soft to the touch - generous 16px card radii, a 0.98 press-scale on every button, 150-180ms transitions - so the interface feels physically pressable rather than clicked. Type is a two-voice pairing: Inter carries every functional surface, and Libre Baskerville appears only where the product turns editorial (the wordmark, pull-quotes, book copy), which keeps the serif meaningful instead of decorative.

The system spans an unusually wide range for one world: a listener's library at one end, a 25-section server admin panel at the other, and a large-touchscreen car shell in between. All three use the same tokens. Admin density is allowed to be dense; it is not allowed to become a different visual world.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-neutral surfaces on an ink base, never navy or brown
One live light source: a cover-tinted radial bloom behind the content
Cover art supplies the colour; chrome stays at 6% fill and 8% hairline
Soft-touch controls: 16px radii, press-scale feedback, 150-180ms easing
Two type voices - Inter functional, Libre Baskerville editorial
Four themes off one token set: dark (home), light, flat/OLED, plus a car shell

rules.name: The Two Warms Rule
rules.body: Ember Coral is functional; Hearth Gold is brand. A control tinted gold is a bug, and a wordmark tinted coral is a bug. They are close in hue on purpose - that is what makes the discipline necessary.

rules.name: The Cover-Supplies-Colour Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour on a library screen comes from artwork, not from UI. If a new component needs colour to be understood, prefer the glow, a surface step, or type weight before reaching for a hue.

rules.name: The Accent-Is-Not-Accent Rule
rules.body: In shadcn's token convention --accent is a neutral hover surface (#322f2b), not the brand accent. Interactive colour is --primary / --ring. See Do's and Don'ts for the live inconsistency this has already caused.

rules.name: The Rare Serif Rule
rules.body: Libre Baskerville appears in the wordmark, pull-quotes, and book prose. It never sets a heading, a button, or a label. Its scarcity is the point.

rules.name: The Tracked Kicker Rule
rules.body: The eyebrow's 0.32em tracking and 300 weight are load-bearing - it is the one place this system is overtly stylish. Keep it wide, keep it light, keep it uppercase.

rules.name: The Single-Lever Rule
rules.body: Left-edge geometry is derived from --sidebar-w. Anything that hardcodes 248px will desynchronise the moment the rail collapses or the car shell mounts.

rules.name: The One Light Source Rule
rules.body: There is a single bloom, behind the content column, tinted by the artwork. Adding a second glow elsewhere on the page breaks the room.

rules.name: The Flat-Theme Rule
rules.body: Flat/OLED is not 'dark with darker colours' - it sets --glow-strength: 0 and removes the atmosphere entirely. Any new effect that depends on the bloom must still read with it switched off.

rules.name: The No-Sharp-Corners Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system has a 0px radius. The smallest corner is 10px, on cover art.

dos: Do use --primary / --ring (Ember Coral #e0654a) for every interactive and stateful colour.
Do reserve Hearth Gold (#bd863f) for the wordmark alone.
Do derive left-edge geometry from --sidebar-w, never from a literal 248px.
Do keep the scale(0.98) press on every new actionable control.
Do design new surfaces against all four themes - dark, light, flat/OLED, and the car shell - since flat sets --glow-strength: 0 and removes the bloom.
Do give every cover a typeset fallback rather than an empty placeholder.
Do honour the 4px spacing cadence and the five-step radius scale.
Do use cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.7, 0.3, 1) for motion; it is the system's only easing curve.
Do let cover art carry the colour on library surfaces.
donts: Don't use --accent for interactive colour. In this system --accent is a neutral hover surface (#322f2b dark / #e7dcc9 light). KNOWN DEFECT: the ported shell in src/styles/design.css reads var(--accent) for .btn-primary, .nav-item.active, .pill.on, .fld:focus and the cover-size slider, so those render warm-grey instead of ember. Do not copy this pattern into new components - use --primary. Fixing the existing rules is tracked work, not settled intent.
Don't add a second glow. There is one light source, behind the content column.
Don't set headings, buttons or labels in Libre Baskerville.
Don't reduce the eyebrow's 0.32em tracking toward a conventional value.
Don't introduce navy or brown surfaces. Warm near-neutrals only - R >= G >= B by a hair.
Don't use a 0px radius anywhere; 10px is the tightest corner in the system.
Don't use chart colours as UI colours.
Don't load a font from a CDN - every face is self-hosted and offline-safe.
Don't add overflow to body; the shell is a fixed grid that scrolls its own content pane.
Don't let admin density drift into a second visual world. /config and /admin may be dense, but they use these tokens.
